title: Introduce compact sample-tiler and quantization policy operator for economical prefetching
author: Samira Kline
release_notes: Adds a new sample-tiler operator and quantization policy controller to improve unit economics by combining lightweight request tiling with conservative quant presets. Backward-compatible; gated behind runtime feature flag 'econ.tiler_v1'.
description: Context: Many workloads have spiky short-sequence requests where neither large batchers nor full prefill policies are optimal. This PR introduces a compact sample-tiler operator that splits incoming request streams into short, topology-aware mini-tiles to increase slot utilization without inflating latency for singletons, and pairs it with a quantization-policy operator that selects conservative quant presets per-tiler based on recent unit-econ telemetry. Motivation: provide an automated, low-risk path to better token unit economics on mixed traffic without changing customer prompts or model contracts. Changes: 1) runtime/operator/sample_tiler: new operator that implements a topology-safe tiling algorithm (max_tile=8, adaptive timeout with workload feedback). 2) runtime/quant/policy: a policy controller that maps tiler signatures to quant presets and rollbacks when quality signals drop. 3) sdk/telemetry: new econ_signals telemetry events + sampling tags used by the policy controller. 4) console: UX hooks to visualize tiler adoption and per-tiler unit-econ. 5) e2e tests + perf microbench harness. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-4921) - [x] unit tests for tiler/sharding logic - [x] perf microbench against 3 sample workloads - [x] backward compatibility checks and runtime flag - [x] smoke deploy to canary - [x] safety fallback: immediate quant rollback and tile dissolution on quality regression Rollout plan: enable feature flag off by default; staged rollout to 10% of traffic in canary, monitor econ_signals (cost/token) and p95 latency for 48h, then 50% and full. Revert plan: runtime flag off + policy controller revert; hotfix script included in ops/scripts/revert_tiler.sh. Compatibility notes: no API surface changes; models and customers unaffected unless they opt-in or rollout turned on. Related work: builds on prefilling and prefetch concepts (see ENG-5038) but focuses on low-latency tiling rather than long prefill. Testing: see commits for unit and integration tests; perf numbers attached in the PR artifacts.

review_comments: Ethan Li (2026-02-15): Please add a perf regression guard that fails gating if p95 latency increases >5% for more than 1h. Also suggest adding a unit test for tile boundary conditions where sequence length==max_tile.

Samira Kline (2026-02-16): Added a guard in policy_controller and added unit test for boundary conditions in test_sample_tiler.py (see commit c12f9aa). Updated perf job to surface p95 deltas in CI artifacts.

Maya Gonzalez (2026-02-17): Suggest clarifying the rollback signal semantics — make sure the policy controller uses quality signals aggregated at model-version granularity to avoid flapping. Also requested docs for ops runbook.
Samira Kline (2026-02-18): Policy controller now aggregates by model/version and uses a 3-sample median window before triggering rollback; ops runbook added at docs/operations/tiler-operator.md.

Oliver Schmidt (2026-02-19): Approval with a minor nit on naming (tile_id -> tiler_id) in one helper; addressed in follow-up commit e9a1c2b. CI green, microbench shows 12-18% token cost improvement on mixed short-seq workload without p95 regression.
